Meshes

6 calls on gfx, generated from the firmware. Every one exists on the device exactly as written here.

The whole-model fast path (engine v11+). One call draws a model: transform, cull, light and rasterise all happen in C.

gfx.mcam

gfx.mcam(cfg)

engine v12

Camera for every gfx.mesh (and gfx.vdraw) until the next call. cfg: x, y, z, yaw, pitch = where the camera is and where it looks focal = pixels per world unit at distance 1 cx, cy = projection centre, usually the canvas centre tier = palette step C adds per lighting tier (stomp's +32/+64 convention, so 32) lx, ly, lz = light direction, normalised fog1, fog2 = distance fog (engine v12): a face past fog1 drops one lighting tier, past fog2 two. The SAME two bands gfx.terrain and gfx.floor fade the ground through, so a model recedes into the haze with the world behind it instead of reading as a sticker. 0 = off. depth = false skips the per-pixel depth test and fills spans with memset. The test costs 2 PSRAM reads + 2 writes per pixel and buys nothing over a FLAT ground, so an app that sorts its models far-to-near should turn it off (~4 ms/frame in Pet Parade). ztest = false (engine v16) still WRITES depth but skips the compare: half the PSRAM traffic, for ground layers the app painter-orders itself. Things that interpenetrate, such as props and the player, keep it.

#argument
1cfgrequired
16 table fields, with defaults
xdefault 0.0
ydefault 0.0
zdefault 3.0
yawdefault 0.0
pitchdefault 0.0
focaldefault 110.0
cxdefault 120.0
cydefault 80.0
tierdefault 32.0
lxdefault -0.32
lydefault -0.24
lzdefault 0.92
fog1default 0.0
fog2default 0.0
depthdefault true
ztestdefault true

gfx.mesh

gfx.mesh(slot, x, y, z [, yaw [, scale [, pitch [, roll [, tier [, col [, smap [, zbias]]]]]]]]) -> faces drawn

engine v16

One call draws the whole model: transform, near-clip, backface cull, directional lighting and a z-buffered span fill against the same depth buffer gfx.terrain / gfx.floor write, so meshes occlude the ground and each other with no sorting and no popping.

roll spins the model about its own forward axis, because yaw and pitch together cannot express a barrel roll. tier defaults to -1 = light it; tier >= 0 forces one lighting tier (flat/emissive). col >= 0 overrides every face colour.

smap (engine v16) > 0 draws the mesh THROUGH that gfx.shademap level, remapping the framebuffer pixels it covers rather than replacing them, which is how real translucent shadows and tints are drawn. zbias (engine v16, world units) is a depth priority: the mesh wins the z-fight against coplanar-ish layers below it, which is what water over terrain and decals on ground need. Affine depth interpolation makes big flat layers fight, and tessellating them alone does not fully fix it.

#argument
1slotrequired
2xrequired
3yrequired
4zrequired
5yawoptional, default 0
6scaleoptional, default 1
7pitchoptional, default 0
8rolloptional, default 0
9tieroptional, default -1
10coloptional, default -1
11smapoptional, default 0
12zbiasoptional, default 0

gfx.mload

gfx.mload(model) -> slot | nil
gfx.mload("name") -> slot | nil

needs asset files engine v16

Upload a model table (the shape each tools/assets gen.py emits, and stomp's lib/models.lua hand-builds): verts = {{x,y,z}, ...} faces = {{a,b,c[,d], col=, nx=, ny=, nz=}, ...} -- 1-based, d = quad parts = { name = {first_face, last_face, px,py,pz}, ... } -- optional Geometry is copied into native arrays, so the Lua tables can be dropped afterwards. Call in vupp.init: it allocates, and the frame budget is real.

Engine v16: load assets/models/ {name}.vmesh straight into the mesh slot, touching zero Lua heap. Model tables of this size are ~15x their binary weight as Lua objects AND vupp.import pins whatever it returns for the life of the app, so a two-thousand-face model as a lib table is a memory bug, not a style choice. Format (little-endian, the tools/assets gen scripts emit it): "VMSH" u8 ver=1, u8 pad, u16 nv, u16 nf, nv * 3*f32 xyz, nf * { u16 a,b,c,d (0-based, d=0xFFFF triangle); u8 col; i8 nx,ny,nz } No parts (rigid models); use the table form when a model needs mpose.

#argument
1namerequired: model.faces: 1..8192 faces

gfx.mpose

gfx.mpose(slot, part, yaw [, pitch [, dx, dy, dz]])

Pose one part about its own pivot, sticky until changed. Parts are 1-based in the order model.parts iterated at load. This is how a character walks without a skeleton: swing the leg parts, bob the body.

#argument
1slotrequired
2partrequired
3yawrequired
4pitchoptional, default 0
5dxoptional, default 0
6dyoptional, default 0
7dzoptional, default 0

gfx.munload

gfx.munload(slot) -> bool

engine v15

Free one mesh slot (engine v15). Lets a screen-based app swap model sets inside the 16-slot budget; unloading a slot mid-frame that a queued gfx.mesh still references is the app's bug.

#argument
1slotrequired

gfx.zclear

gfx.zclear()

engine v16

Reset the depth buffer to far (engine v16). For mesh scenes with no ground pass (cards, mirrors) that still want z-tested models.
